clue.text: Become terrible Republican party spearhead for reform

parts.note: the GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

indicators.note: spearhead is to be re-formed, its letters remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A call for the Republicans to have a new leader if things go badly.
explanation.walkthrough: GOP is the American Republican Party's nickname; SPEARHEAD rearranged gives PEARSHAPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To go pear-shaped is a British idiom for a plan going badly wrong.

clue.text: Girl eating cheese is an angel

indicators.note: the girl eats the cheese, so it goes inside her

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A girl tucking into some cheese is described as an angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is the archangel who announces births in the Bible, a named example of an angel.

clue.text: Expert live analysis

parts.note: a pro is an expert, a professional
to be is to live, to exist

explanation.surface: An expert gives a live commentary breaking down a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' reads as an adjective (live analysis on air) but is the verb, to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough investigation, so it stands for a close examination.

clue.text: Stars with capital getting lawyer from New York

parts.note: and means together with
Rome is the capital of Italy
DA, District Attorney, is an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: Celebrities travel to the capital to consult a New York attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Posh boys regularly rejected in part of London

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters picked are read in reverse order
every other letter is taken, at regular intervals

parts.note: every second letter of these words

explanation.surface: Upper-class young men are turned away from a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London known for nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district in London's West End, so it is an example of an area of the city.

clue.text: Former Soviet leader in an audible decline?

parts.note: taken as it stands

indicators.note: audible means we hear the words, so they stand for a name said the same way

parts.note: a drop-off is a decline or fall

explanation.surface: A question whether a past Soviet leader suffered a noticeable decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'an drop-off' sounds like the Russian surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Andropov led the Soviet Union from 1982 to 1984 as General Secretary.

clue.text: Perhaps Ben is making something last longer?

indicators.note: Ben is followed by these letters in the singer's name, so the full name with Ben taken away is what remains

parts.note: Ben E. King, the American soul singer, is one example of a Ben; strip his first name and what is left completes the clue

explanation.surface: A question whether someone called Ben is stretching something out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben E. King sang 'Stand By Me': the clue says a Ben 'is' these letters, since Ben followed by them names the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke out is to make a supply stretch further than it otherwise would.

clue.text: Over the phone, deal in cooked meat for cooler friend

indicators.note: heard over the phone, a word is known only by its sound

parts.note: to deal in goods is to sell them

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or altered, so the letters of meat are reworked

explanation.surface: A phone-ordered deal for a cooked-meat product, sold to a cooler friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is slang for prison, not something cold; a cellmate is a friend made in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooler is slang for a prison, so a companion inside it shares a cell with you.

clue.text: Beach sport is uplifting around November

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the letter for November
in a down clue, lifting up turns the word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: darts is a pub sport
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A beach sport proves cheering around the month of November.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is a literary word for the shore, the sandy edge of the sea.

clue.text: Start to build two outhouses to conceal entrance to duplex, creating carnage

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter used

indicators.note: the two outhouses hide the next letter between them

parts.note: a loo and a shed are two outbuildings

indicators.note: the entrance is the opening, the first letter

parts.note: first letter used

explanation.surface: Instructions for a builder: put up two outhouses screening the duplex entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: A loo is British slang for a toilet, once often an outbuilding; 'creating' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshed is killing or violence on a large scale, the same as a slaughter.

clue.text: Write about boring sex, which is awkward

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the turned word goes inside

parts.note: it is an old euphemism for sex or sex appeal

indicators.note: about means turned round, so pen is read backwards

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A critic complains that writing about dull sex is clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull' but means drilling into; 'it' is old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, clumsy, so it matches a socially or physically awkward manner.

clue.text: Nationalist evicted from refined Spar food store

indicators.note: the letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: nice can mean refined or subtle, as in a nice distinction
to spar is to box

explanation.surface: A nationalist is thrown out of a smart Spar food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a chain of British convenience stores, which makes 'food store' look like part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is an old name for a refrigerator, a cabinet where food is kept cold.

clue.text: Log on with aim to corrupt country

indicators.note: corrupting the letters spoils their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hacker logs on intending to damage a nation's systems.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongolia is a landlocked nation in East Asia between Russia and China.

clue.text: Pay attention to Flash Gordon's origin being leaked

indicators.note: the letter leaks out, so it is lost from the word

parts.note: to glisten is to flash or shine

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter used

explanation.surface: A news item about Flash Gordon's backstory being leaked to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Flash Gordon is the comic-strip space hero, but the two words are split: Flash is the verb and Gordon gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to give heed, the verb equivalent of attending to someone.

clue.text: Outrage about broken arm being national emblem

indicators.note: the outrage goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: shock is a feeling of outrage

indicators.note: broken means the letters of arm are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Anger as a national symbol is damaged, with an arm broken off a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock, a three-leaved clover, is the symbolic plant of Ireland.

clue.text: Message from friends on vacation, perhaps, after vehicle died

definitions.text: Message from friends on vacation, perhaps

parts.note: post is a Latin prefix meaning after
a car is a vehicle
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A note from friends on holiday sent after their car broke down.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers traditionally send a postcard, a picture card, home to friends.

clue.text: Collections of models resistant to change

indicators.note: the letters are to be changed, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Groups of fashion models refuse to adapt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' suggests catwalk fashion, but these are scale models of railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a toy railway, a set of miniature engines, carriages and track.

clue.text: Help medics to stray

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off, so the letters drift out of order

explanation.surface: A call for assistance to stop doctors wandering away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help' is a noun here: domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, someone employed as hired help in the home.

clue.text: Stop and help returning father and son

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father and son come back to stop and lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is the noun, a set of organ pipes, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is one of the main stops on a pipe organ, controlling a rank of pipes.

clue.text: Mostly talk about plate thrown in Athens?

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is cut

parts.note: to discuss is to talk about

explanation.surface: Mostly talk about a plate hurled in Greece, as at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Plate-smashing at Greek parties is the decoy; the discus throw began in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is a heavy disc hurled in athletics, an event dating to the ancient Greek games.

clue.text: Cavalier wanting the Parisian's loving touch

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so these letters are missing

parts.note: a cavalier attitude is careless and offhand
le is the French word for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A dashing cavalier yearns for the tender caress of a Parisian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' looks like a royalist soldier but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle, affectionate stroke, a tender physical gesture.

clue.text: Description of fluid in males

parts.note: the adjective used in the phrase for the fluid men produce, but also meaning highly influential

explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes the fluid in a fixed phrase; its everyday sense, groundbreaking, is the hidden joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to semen, as in the medical phrase for the fluid ejaculated by men.

clue.text: Unfortunately, her plans change

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Sadly, a woman's plans have to be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrapnel is British slang for small coins; 'change' is the noun, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang shrapnel is loose coins, the heavy small money in a pocket.

clue.text: An international lecturer is in danger

parts.note: per means a or an, as in five pounds per hour

explanation.surface: An academic who teaches abroad finds herself at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious risk of harm, the same idea as jeopardy.

clue.text: Song is abomination without two altos

indicators.note: without means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: an anathema is something detested, an abomination
A is the abbreviation for alto in choral music, so two altos are two A's

explanation.surface: A choir piece is deemed dreadful when sung without its two altos.
explanation.walkthrough: Two of the three As go; the first stays.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a choral composition or a rousing hymn, so it is a type of song.

clue.text: Island in Hawaii becomes self-governing state

indicators.note: the island goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: HI is the US postal abbreviation for Hawaii
an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames

explanation.surface: An island in Hawaii gains independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island' wants to be the definition; it gives AIT, and the answer is a country, not an island name.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti, sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, is an independent republic.

clue.text: Save European with no clothes on

parts.note: bar and save both mean except

explanation.surface: A European naturist saves money by going without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means naked, uncovered, as in bare skin.

clue.text: Sore back precludes fencing

indicators.note: back means the letters run backwards
fencing means enclosing: the word fences in the letters wanted

parts.note: the word containing the answer, backwards

explanation.surface: An injured back rules out taking part in fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like the sport but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore on skin or a membrane such as the stomach lining.

clue.text: Maybe Arthur Miller seethed, suppressed by tense Scotsman

indicators.note: held down by, so placed inside the following letters

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
Ian is a typical Scottish first name
to seethe is to rage

explanation.surface: Arthur Miller fumed while kept quiet by a tense Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Miller wrote tragic plays such as Death of a Salesman, so he is an example of a writer of tragedies.

clue.text: Lock sleeping criminal in steel bars

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are out of line

explanation.surface: Put a slumbering criminal behind steel bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steel bars' looks like a prison cell; it is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A glockenspiel is a percussion instrument of tuned metal plates struck with hammers.
